basis: Actual renderDrawer output with repository compiled database and literal independently reviewed source qualifications. HTML assertion verifies content, not browser layout or human review.

cases.quote: Supports in 3D printing need to be removed manually a posteriori, which may leave marks and can take time for more complex structures.
cases.scope: General removal limitation in own HIPS article; no measured force/time or assurance on this exact geometry.

cases.quote: High Impact Polystyrene (HIPS), as its name indicates, has a very high shock resistance. This resistance also makes it suited as a base 3D printing material, especially for press tools.
cases.scope: General HIPS declarative maker context within own article; no exact-product press-tool load, impact/lifetime test or qualified use. Not a material suitability pass.

cases.quote: When submerged in limonene, HIPS completely dissolves in about 24 hours, and doesn’t leave any residue.
cases.scope: Declarative general HIPS maker claim, not a described exact-product removal test. Approximate24hours; concentration, temperature, geometry and protocol missing. Does not turn prior exposure-only caption into a transferable complete-removal guarantee.

cases.quote: commonly used in automotives (Li & MH batteries, connectors, electrical materials ...) and outdoor products (solar panels connections...).
cases.scope: Own electrical applications paragraph; maker claimed uses only, no automotive/battery/solar service protocol or qualification.

cases.quote: A heating plate is necessary during printing (between 100 and 140°C) and the filament is extruded at a temperature range from 260 to 280°C.
cases.scope: Internal conflict: own Properties table prints Plate Temp. 130–150 °C. Existing page profile P0721 retained; neither paragraph priority nor unprinted chronology settles the range.
cases.locator: p. 1: Applications paragraph, conflicting bed range

cases.scope: Own recommendation retains 0.5 mm and strict >0.4 mm wording; not a hardened-nozzle claim, not converted to >=0.4 or a profile scalar.

cases.quote: In order to guarantee good printing conditions dehydrate Nanovia Insublend at 60°c for 4 hours or longer, when the spools has been exposed to moisture for an extended period.
cases.scope: Own drying instruction, conditional on prolonged moisture exposure, lower bound4hours. Conflicts with current page/profile80 °C/4h. No replacement, narrowed time or service-moisture/hydrolysis result inferred.
cases.locator: p. 2: Storage drying bullet; French p1 corroborates

cases.quote: For a better print quality, desactivate the retraction option on your 3D printer
cases.scope: Own printing advice; no printer/nozzle/path or quantified result. Preserve source spelling; not universally proven optimal settings.
cases.locator: p. 2: Printing retraction bullet; French p1 corroborates

cases.quote: We recommend printing Nanovia Insublend in a room equipped with air extraction or by using appropriate breathing equipment. Whilst printing Nanovia Insublend produces a VOC derivative of styrene.
cases.scope: English own processing precaution; French p1 names generic COV only. No measured emissions, airborne concentration, validated ventilation or gas-limit qualification.
